bib.title: Hard Prompts Made Easy: Gradient-Based Discrete Optimization for Prompt Tuning and Discovery

question: Can hard (interpretable, portable) text prompts be learned efficiently by gradient-based optimisation, for both text-to-image and text-to-text tasks?
hypothesis: Keeping a continuous soft prompt as the iterate while evaluating gradients at its nearest-neighbour projection (PEZ) finds better and more transferable hard prompts than projecting after every update (AutoPrompt, FluentPrompt).
contributions: A simple scheme for learning hard prompts using continuous optimisation (PEZ), adapting lessons from quantized-network optimisation.
Hard prompts for image generation that perform competitively with specialised prompt tools using far fewer tokens.
Learned hard prompts that perform well on language classification, out-perform other text optimisation schemes, and transfer across networks, more so with fluency regularisation.

method.summary: PEZ keeps a continuous prompt embedding P, projects it to nearest vocabulary embeddings P', computes the task gradient at P' and applies it to P, with a final projection. Applied to CLIP prompt inversion (prompts for Stable Diffusion) and to few-shot and full-data prompt tuning of GPT-2 Large for classification, with transfer to larger LMs.
method.task: hard prompt optimisation: CLIP prompt inversion for text-to-image; prompt tuning for text classification

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.split: hold-out set of 5000 examples for early stopping; reports validation accuracy

datasets.name: Amazon Polarity
datasets.split: hold-out set of 5000 examples for early stopping; validation accuracy

datasets.name: AGNEWS
datasets.split: few-shot: k=2 or k=4 examples per class as train set, equal-size holdout, validated on full validation set

other.use: frozen, drives prompt optimisation; shares text encoder with Stable Diffusion v2
reference model for CLIP score, not used in optimisation
frozen; source model for prompt optimisation

training.objective: Image: L(P,x)=1-S(f(P),g(x)) cosine similarity of CLIP text and image embeddings. Text: L=(1-lambda_fluency)L_task+lambda_fluency L_fluency, lambda=0.003 (0.03 for few-shot AGNEWS). Distillation: L=1-Sim(f(P_target),f(P)).
training.lr: image: 0.1; text (Table 5): best of 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 for PEZ and 1, 3, 10 for AutoPrompt_SGD/FluentPrompt
training.steps: image: 3000; text transfer: 5000 steps on GPT-2 Large
training.seq_len: image: 8 prompt tokens for main PEZ result (16 to 22 judged best generalising); text: 10 prompt tokens prepended for Table 5, 3 appended for few-shot
training.wall_clock: each few-shot run takes about 5 minutes
training.seeds: image: 5 seeds; Table 5: 5 seeds; few-shot: 100 seeds

other.init: prompt embeddings sampled from real vocabulary embeddings; text-task prompt tokens initialised with label tokens (footnote 4)
other.early_stopping: hold-out set of 5000 examples, evaluated every 100 steps

inference.samples: Image: 100 images per dataset, CLIP score averaged over 5 seeds. Transfer: top five prompts by average validation accuracy per method.
inference.prompting: Templates: SST-2/Amazon '<s>It was <mask>' verbalizer positive/negative; AGNEWS '<s>It was about <mask>' verbalizer politics, sports, business, technology. Style transfer uses 'a tiger in the style of {}' etc.

metrics.name: CLIP score
metrics.definition: cosine similarity under OpenCLIP-ViT/G between target image and image generated by Stable Diffusion from the learned prompt

metrics.name: Validation accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy of the LM with learned prompt and template/verbalizer

baselines: CLIP Interrogator (with and without BLIP, 8/16/32/~77 tokens)
eval.protocol: Image: mean over 100 images and 5 seeds per dataset. Text: standard error over 5 prompts or seeds; few-shot over 100 seeds with early stopping. No significance tests.

limits: Learned prompts still contain several un-interpretable tokens (Conclusion).
Hard prompts may extract harmful phrases or sensitive content from training data; not observed.
Soft prompts remain clearly stronger in accuracy (93.35 vs 88.05 SST-2; 79.93 vs 74.15 few-shot).
Image evaluation uses CLIP similarity only, no human study; no significance tests; 100 images per dataset.
Transfer tested only from GPT-2 Large to a few older LMs (up to 6.7B); no hardware or compute stated.
Safety: method can evade token-level content filters.
